Action Plan:
1. Start antibiotic for presumed uncomplicated cystitis: nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim, 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (dose and route not documented).
2. Increase oral fluid intake; cranberry juice may help symptomatically.
3. Avoid sexual intercourse until symptoms resolve; continue condom use afterward.
4. Safety-net: seek care if fever develops, back/flank pain occurs, or if feeling systemically unwell (concern for ascending infection).
5. Follow-up: if symptoms are not improved by the end of this week, call or return for reassessment.
6. Pregnancy: if any concern about pregnancy or if symptoms persist, perform a pregnancy test to rule out pregnancy.
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: Pain with urination for a few days.
- History of presenting complaint:
  - Dysuria described as stinging; began a few days ago.
  - Intermittent lower abdominal cramping discomfort associated with urination.
  - One episode of a small amount of blood in urine earlier today.
  - Malodorous urine.
  - Denies increased urinary frequency.
  - Denies flank/back pain, fever, nausea, vomiting.
  - Bowel movements normal; denies diarrhea.
  - Denies vaginal discharge.
- Gynecologic/sexual history:
  - Sexually active with a boyfriend for a couple of months.
  - Uses condoms.
  - Last STD screen: never.
  - Last menstrual period: “a couple of weeks ago”; clinician documented “three weeks ago” (conflict noted).
  - Denies likelihood of pregnancy.
- Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
- Medications:
  - Over-the-counter bicarbonate recently for symptom relief; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies:
  - Clindamycin — causes swelling.
- Social history:
  - 19-year-old college student (biology).
  - Lives in a flat with friends.
  - Non-smoker.
  - Alcohol: drinks socially on weekends.
- Family history: No known kidney, bladder, or gastrointestinal diseases.

Objective:
- No vital signs recorded.
- No physical examination documented (telehealth; examination not performed).
- Investigations: None performed or ordered during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Dysuria with lower abdominal discomfort:
   - Assessment: Acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection (cystitis).
   - Investigations planned: None documented.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim, 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (dose and route not documented).
     - Increase oral fluids; cranberry juice may provide symptomatic relief.
     - Avoid sexual intercourse until symptoms have resolved; continue condom use thereafter.
   - Safety advice:
     - Return/seek care urgently if fever, back/flank pain, or worsening systemic symptoms occur (concern for ascending infection).
   - Follow-up:
     - If not improved by end of this week, call or return for reassessment.

2. Pregnancy status consideration:
   - Assessment: Patient reports low likelihood of pregnancy; last menstrual period timing noted as “a couple of weeks ago” vs “three weeks ago” (conflict noted).
   - Investigations planned: Home pregnancy test if any concern about pregnancy or if symptoms persist.
   - Treatment planned: None.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - No urinalysis (dipstick) or urine culture obtained.
  - No vital signs.
  - No pregnancy test performed.
  - No STI screening offered despite new sexual relationship and no prior screening.
  - Antibiotic choice (which specific agent), dose (mg), and route not documented.
  - No documentation of renal function assessment prior to nitrofurantoin consideration.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Last menstrual period documented as “a couple of weeks ago” vs “three weeks ago” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Minor audio interruptions/clarifications; key clinical details were captured.
